cluster_summary: This cluster covers injection vulnerabilities (JDBC parameter injection, JNDI scheme injection, SQL injection) caused by incomplete blacklists, missing scheme or prefix validation, or direct string concatenation of user input into sensitive constructs. The majority of issues stem from assuming user-controlled data is safe when building JDBC URLs or SQL queries without proper validation, canonicalization, or parameterization.
guideline_text: Trace untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata into deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation. Report code paths where allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization.

mechanism.missing_guard: allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization
mechanism.name: untrusted deserialization with attacker-controlled type graph
mechanism.sink_shape: deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation
mechanism.source_shape: untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Expand the blacklist to cover all known dangerous parameters and protocols, apply the check after full URL assembly and URL-decoding, and use robust regex that matches parameter names regardless of context.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete or misapplied blacklist for JDBC connection parameters
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application relies on a blacklist to filter dangerous JDBC URL parameters, but the blacklist is missing entries (e.g., socketFactory, autoDeserialize, iiop), applied too early (before URL assembly or decoding), or uses overly restrictive regex patterns, allowing bypass.
